history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration ensure that the Office of Information and Communications Technology, together with respective entities, updates the cloud strategy in a timely manner to align it with the latest information and communications technology landscape and business requirements, enhances public cloud resource utilization and implements cost-saving measures, as appropriate.
history.administration_response: The Administration considers the recommendation to be implemented and requests its closure. The role of the Office of Information and Communications Technology is to ensure that the relevant contractual arrangements are in place and that the cloud strategy is updated, promulgated and implemented. The Office believes that it has successfully performed its role in this regard and has provided evidence to that end. The utilization of cloud resources is a business decision made by entities. Cloud utilization will always be variable and will change constantly. Details on the variable nature of the utilization of cloud resources have been provided. Given that there are effective contracts in place and as a new cloud strategy has been approved and promulgated, the Office requests that this recommendation be closed.
history.board_assessment: Given that the Board could not determine the extent of the improvement of cloud utilization from the details provided, the Board will request further evidence during the next audit. The Board considers the recommendation to be under implementation.

history.sg_progress: The Office of Information and Communications Technology has updated and published the cloud strategy following a broad consultative process. The revised strategy – cloud strategy 2.0 – is aligned with the current ICT landscape and evolving business requirements, ensuring the effective utilization of public cloud resources and the implementation of cost-saving measures. Cloud strategy 2.0 introduces a hybrid cloud model that enhances scalability through dynamic resource allocation based on performance, cost and compliance needs. It also promotes operational flexibility by enabling the seamless migration of workloads between private and public cloud environments in response to changing business demands. The Administration considers this recommendation to be implemented and requests its closure by the Board.
